claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produced under standard melt-spinning conditions has limited amorphous retention.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has a complex thermal response during heating.
Increasing the melt-spinning cooling rate will suppress the formation of crystallization nuclei in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Suppression of crystallization nuclei will enhance amorphous retention.
Enhanced rapid cooling will improve stability during subsequent moderate reheating relative to standard processing.
Increasing melt-spinning speed or modifying mold design can produce a significantly higher solidification cooling rate.
A cooling rate above a critical threshold is required to suppress nucleation and avoid crystallization.
A higher cooling rate will reduce the density of residual crystalline nuclei.
A higher cooling rate will reduce the size of residual crystalline nuclei.
Reduced residual crystalline nuclei will produce a more uniform amorphous structure.
Rapid cooling limits atomic rearrangement and freezes in a disordered structure.
Minimizing early-stage crystalline clusters extends the temperature range over which the glassy state is maintained during reheating.
Enhanced rapid cooling will yield a higher amorphous-phase fraction than standard cooling.
Enhanced rapid cooling will delay crystallization onset during subsequent heating.
Cooling below the required threshold will fail to produce the predicted improvements.
Extreme reheating rates may trigger unwanted crystallization and negate the improved thermal stability.
